haiku-low.q1: MySQL commits first, with a pending row in the same transaction, then one Postgres copy is tried. If Postgres fails, the caller still sees success.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the target's version is lower than the incoming version, and the id is not tombstoned. The copy takes a lock on the id first.
haiku-low.q3: Every instance must show write_mode=mysql in app_flag_value first. The document gives no maximum time that instances may disagree.
haiku-low.q4: It reads the replica in 2,000-row batches. If replica lag exceeds 5 seconds, it waits 10 seconds and rechecks before each batch.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: one clean comparer pass before each raise to 1, 10, 50, 100. Source move: reads at 100% on Postgres for 3 days, and last comparer pass clean.
haiku-low.q6: A pending row in the MySQL pending table records that Postgres is behind. The sweeper retries the copy every 10 seconds and deletes the row after success.
haiku-low.q7: Copies lock the user id and skip tombstoned ids. Erasure writes a tombstone, so a late copy cannot re-create the deleted user.
haiku-low.q8: Progress is the last completed id in MySQL backfill_progress, saved after each batch commits. It stops at the last id; the comparer starts then.
haiku-low.q9: The comparer finds differences by reading both tables by id. Each counted difference, confirmed against both primaries, is added to pending so the sweeper repairs it.
haiku-low.q10: Every instance must show paused before the drain, then pg, so none writes first-source. If the pause passes 80 seconds, revert to mysql.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres assigns new ids, its sequence set above MySQL's max id plus 1,000. After rollback, MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT is set above the max Postgres id.
haiku-low.q12: Every Postgres write is copied to MySQL via pending rows for 14 days. Rollback runs the five-step procedure. The option ends at step 9, pg_only.

sonnet.q1: MySQL (source) commits first, with a pending row in the same transaction; then one copy to Postgres is tried. If Postgres fails, the caller still sees success (request not failed); the sweeper retries.
sonnet.q2: Only if the target's version is lower than the incoming version (also inserts if missing; skipped if the id is tombstoned; done under a lock on that user id).
sonnet.q3: app_flag_value{flag="users.write_mode"} must show `mysql` on every instance. How long instances can disagree after a flag change: NOT STATED.
sonnet.q4: It reads from the MySQL replica (not primary) in 2,000-row batches in id order; before each batch, if mysql_replica_lag_seconds > 5 it waits 10 seconds and rechecks.
sonnet.q5: Reads: step 5 clean (one full comparer pass with zero counted differences); raise read_from_pg stepwise 1, 10, 50, 100, waiting for a clean comparer pass before each raise. Source switch: reads at 100% on Postgres for 3 days (hold starts when every instance shows 100) and the last comparer pass clean.
sonnet.q6: A pending row (one per user id still to copy), kept in the source database (MySQL), written in the same transaction as the change. The sweeper (every 10 seconds) copies pending ids to Postgres and deletes the pending row after success.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones: erasure writes a tombstone in the source in the same transaction as the delete; every copy skips tombstoned ids, and the sweeper writes a tombstone to the target and deletes the target row if the source row is gone. Copies also take a per-user-id lock.
sonnet.q8: In backfill_progress in MySQL, storing the last completed id, saved after each batch commits (each batch is copied to Postgres in one transaction; if Postgres fails, progress is not saved; reruns are idempotent). It stops at the last id (step 5 starts once the backfill reaches the last id).
sonnet.q9: The comparer, which reads both tables by id in batches and compares id, version and fields. A difference counts only if no pending row exists for the id and rows still differ when re-read from MySQL primary and Postgres (ids in only one table count unless pending or tombstoned). Counted differences are added to pending so the sweeper repairs them; results go to the job log and a metric.
sonnet.q10: Set write_mode=paused (writes get a retryable 503), wait until every instance shows paused, then wait longer than the longest write timeout, drain MySQL pending to Postgres, set the sequence, then set pg; writes resume once every instance shows pg. If it runs long: a failed drain is retried and the pause continues; if the pause is still open at 80 seconds, set write_mode=mysql (as long as pg has not been set); pause max 90 seconds.
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns new ids, via its users id sequence set to the larger of MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT and its max id, plus 1,000. After a rollback, MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT is set above the max Postgres id so MySQL never reuses an id.
sonnet.q12: Each write commits to Postgres with a pending row and the sweeper copies it to MySQL (same copy rule); the comparer keeps running; tombstones in both. Rollback: set read_from_pg=0; run step 7's pause (sub-steps 1 and 2); drain Postgres pending rows into MySQL; set MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT above max Postgres id; set write_mode=mysql. The option ends at step 9 (write_mode=pg_only, allowed at least 14 days after step 7), after which rollback can no longer be lossless.
